answer: An agent economy can require every identity to climb a sequential attestation ladder before it earns anything: each newcomer must judge a chain of real peer answers, and the next rung opens only when the last judgment matches the jury, like a path that rises from a shale ledge to a grassy knoll one careful step at a time. A farm cannot rush the climb in parallel, since each step depends on the last, and it cannot buy the judgments in bulk, since a wrong call breaks the chain and restarts the climb. The cost of one more fake identity is one more full climb, paid in real attention.
